description: Support explicit manifest declarations for re-export shims, adapters, and duplicated types pending merge; auto-detect undeclared-transitional patterns as warning conflicts; enforce two-tier strictness (--mid-migration tolerates, --strict errors when expires_when predicates fire).

requirements.description: Cartographer must support explicit manifest declarations for transitional architecture states including re-export shims, adapters, and duplicated types pending merge (AC-TRANSITIONAL-DECL). Undeclared transitional patterns must be auto-detected and emitted as warning-severity conflicts (AC-TRANSITIONAL-DETECT). The expires_when predicate in transitional declarations must be evaluated at analysis time to determine if a transitional state has expired (AC-TRANSITIONAL-EXPIRES). Two strictness modes must be supported: --mid-migration (tolerates declared transitional patterns) and --strict (errors when expires_when predicates fire) (AC-TRANSITIONAL-STRICTNESS).
requirements.title: Transitional State Lifecycle — Declarations, Detection, and Strictness Modes

validation.notes: AC-TRANSITIONAL-DECL: Manifest parser correctly reads transitional declaration fields (pattern, expires_when, description)
AC-TRANSITIONAL-DETECT: A re-export shim not declared in the manifest produces a warning conflict of type undeclared-transitional
AC-TRANSITIONAL-EXPIRES: An expires_when predicate based on date is evaluated against current time and fires when past due
AC-TRANSITIONAL-EXPIRES: An expires_when predicate based on a graph condition (e.g., symbol removed) is evaluated against the current graph
AC-TRANSITIONAL-STRICTNESS: --mid-migration mode allows declared transitional patterns without surfacing them as errors
AC-TRANSITIONAL-STRICTNESS: --strict mode converts expired transitional declarations into error-severity conflicts
Fixture scenario with a declared re-export shim: --mid-migration produces no conflict; --strict after expiry produces an error conflict
Fixture scenario with an undeclared adapter pattern: auto-detect produces a warning conflict regardless of strictness mode
Transitional declaration round-trip: declared in manifest → loaded → evaluated → result matches expected strictness output
A team mid-migration can run in --mid-migration mode without noise from known transitional patterns
Expired transitional states are not silently ignored; --strict ensures they are surfaced before merge

title: Transitional State Lifecycle
